sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.name: ls
toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

content.text:
When pi sends a request through the anthropic-cc provider, what happens to the request body between the point where the stock Anthropic code builds it and the HTTP call? Walk me through the functions that rewrite it, in the order they run.

This is a read-only question: do not modify any file. End your reply with your final answer between a line `<answer>` and a line `</answer>`.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). # Pi Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own. Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other way around. Customize Pi with [extensions](docs/extensions.md), [skills](docs/skills.md), [prompt templates](docs/prompt-templates.md), and [themes](docs/themes.md). Bundle them as [Pi packages](docs/packages.md) and share via npm or git. Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode. Ask Pi to build what you want, or install a package that does it your way. Use Pi [interactively](docs/usage.md), automate it in [print or JSON mode](docs/cli.md), control it over [RPC](docs/rpc.md), or build apps with the [Pi TypeScript SDK](docs/sdk.md). See [OpenClaw](https://github.com/OpenClaw/OpenClaw) for a real-world integration. ## Getting started Install the command-line interface: ```bash curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows: ```shell powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The installer pins all dependencies and updates Pi with `pi update`. Alternatively, install directly with npm, which does not pin transitive dependencies: ```bash npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ``` Pi requires Node.js 22.19 or newer. The macOS, Linux, and Windows installers can install it if needed. Pi does not require dependency lifecycle scripts for a normal npm installation. On macOS and Linux, Nix users can install the latest release with `nix profile add github:earendil-works/pi/stable`. See the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md#1-install-pi) for updating and pinning releases. Start Pi in the directory where you want it to work: ```bash cd /path/to/project pi ``` For a built-in AI provider, run `/login` inside Pi to connect a subscription or API key. Then give Pi a task. See the [documentation](docs/index.md) for full setup and usage instructions. ## Share your OSS coding agent sessions If you use Pi for open source work, please share your coding agent sessions. Public OSS session data helps improve models, prompts, tools, and evaluations using real development workflows. For the full explanation, see [this post on X](https://x.com/badlogicgames/status/2037811643774652911). To publish sessions, use [`badlogic/pi-share-hf`](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-share-hf) using a Hugging Face account and the Hugging Face CLI. - [Demo video](https://x.com/badlogicgames/status/2041151967695634619) on how to publish Pi sessions - Published Pi development sessions: [`badlogicgames/pi-mono` on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/badlogicgames/pi-mono). ## Development Clone the repository, install its dependencies, and run Pi from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/earendil-works/pi cd pi npm install --ignore-scripts ./pi-test.sh ``` `pi-test.sh` can be called from any directory and preserves the caller's working directory. Before submitting changes, run: ```bash npm run check ./test.sh ``` Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull request. It defines the contribution gate, issue quality bar, and required checks. Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/AGENTS.md) for repository-specific implementation, testing, dependency, and release rules. ## License MIT

<answer>
The live provider path is **`streamAnthropicCc` → vendored `streamSimpleAnthropic` / `streamAnthropic` → SDK → fetch**. The provider installs a wrapped `onPayload` hook; that is where most rewriting happens.

### In execution order

1. **Stock `buildParams()` constructs the Anthropic body.**  
   In `src/anthropic-cc/vendor/anthropicStock.ts:398`, stock code builds `model`, `messages`, tools, system blocks, thinking settings, etc. It then awaits the provider’s wrapped `onPayload`.

2. **`applyAnthropicCcBodyOverrides()` applies the initial provider rewrite.**  
   Called from `src/anthropic-cc/stream.ts:57`, implemented in `src/anthropic-cc/overrides.ts:308`. Internally, in order:

   - **`applyAnthropicCcIdentityOverrides()`** preserves existing metadata and supplies `metadata.user_id` only if missing. It **replaces the stock `system` array** using **`buildAnthropicCcSystemPrelude()`**: a billing-header text block, the Claude Agent SDK identity block, then the user’s system prompt.
     - For OAuth, **`sanitizeAnthropicCcSystemPrompt()`** strips recognized Pi identity statements and rewrites recognized documentation references to neutral aliases.
     - System text is Unicode-sanitized. The stock cache policy is reused, but only the **last new system block** receives `cache_control`.
   - Adds baseline `context_management` and `thinking` **only when those fields are absent**.
   - **`applyAnthropicCcToolPolicy()`** rewrites both top-level tools and inline `tool_addition` definitions. It removes `__pi_deferred_placeholder__` definitions; **`applyAnthropicCcToolDefinitionPolicy()`** removes `cache_control` and `defer_loading`, and forces `eager_input_streaming: true`.
   - Adaptive thinking without `block_binding` gets `display: "omitted"`. Bound adaptive thinking is left alone.
   - Existing `output_config` is preserved exactly. Otherwise it uses a baseline default, or a model-specific adaptive default—currently `effort: "xhigh"` for Opus 4.7/4.8 and Fable 5.

3. **The wrapper captures the established user identity, then calls the caller’s `onPayload`.**  
   In `src/anthropic-cc/stream.ts`, it saves the resulting string `metadata.user_id`—or the file-backed fallback—**before** awaiting `callerOnPayload(next, modelArg)`.  
   A non-`undefined` return replaces the payload; otherwise mutations to the supplied object remain effective.

4. **`applyAnthropicCcToolPolicy()` runs again.**  
   This occurs **after the caller hook**, so caller-added or replaced tools still get the eager/non-deferred policy, including inline definitions.

5. **`sanitizeAnthropicCcRequestParams()` performs final compatibility cleanup.**  
   Defined in `src/anthropic-cc/request.ts:148`, it:
   - Removes `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` for Opus 4.7/4.8; otherwise removes only `temperature` when model compatibility says it is unsupported.
   - Converts legacy `thinking.type: "enabled"` to `"adaptive"` and removes `budget_tokens` for Opus 4.7/4.8 or models with `forceAdaptiveThinking`.
   - Removes trailing assistant prefill for the listed Claude 5 and Claude 4.6–4.8 models. It accounts for a trailing managed-effort control message and removes the prefill’s preceding managed-effort control when present.
   - Deletes `context_management` if thinking is neither enabled nor adaptive.

6. **The wrapper restores `metadata.user_id`.**  
   It merges the sanitized metadata but overwrites `user_id` with the identity captured in step 3. Thus the caller hook cannot replace or remove that established identity. The full body-override pass is **not** rerun: only tool policy, compatibility sanitization, and identity restoration follow the caller hook.

7. **Stock code forces streaming, then the SDK serializes and sends it.**  
   `src/anthropic-cc/vendor/anthropicStock.ts:403` calls:
   ```ts
   client.messages.create({ ...params, stream: true }, requestOptions)
   ```
   The installed SDK’s `Messages.create()` extracts any `user_profile_id` into an HTTP header; the remaining body is JSON-encoded. Finally, **`withMessagesBetaQuery()`** adds `beta=true` to the messages URL when absent and strips the SDK helper header—it does **not** rewrite the body.

The standalone builders in `request.ts` are separate helpers, not the registered live streaming path described above. If stock’s strict-tool fallback triggers, it rebuilds the parameters and reruns this payload-hook sequence before sending again.
</answer>
